cover.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: original editorial science review cover, wide 16:9 composition, no typography.
Primary request: an intimate, anatomically inspired but clearly conceptual micro-landscape about adult hippocampal neurogenesis and the difficulty of joining an existing neural circuit.
Scene and subject: a narrow curved, open C-shaped layered band of densely nestled small rounded cell bodies, suggesting the dentate gyrus rather than an entire brain. From a small limited region along the inside edge, one delicate pale apricot young neuron extends short sparse dendritic branches upward into a much larger surrounding canopy of mature branching neurons. The established branches are rich dark blue-green, organically varied and clearly more extensive than the young cell. A few warm brown branching trunks surround the curved band. Allow the emerging neuron and nearby space to remain legible and central. The scene should evoke a living neural tissue niche and the relationship of new growth to established circuitry, without a medical before/after narrative.
Style and material: sophisticated hand-cut layered paper relief with matte gouache edges, visible fine paper fibres, restrained organic shapes, gentle raking daylight and deep natural shadows. Precise, calm, curious editorial mood. Ivory ground, deep petrol teal, dusty terracotta, muted apricot, warm charcoal. Distinct asymmetrical composition and generous quiet space, not a rigid infographic.
Scientific boundaries: conceptual simplified hippocampal geometry, not a faithful histological section. Do not depict a whole glowing brain, technology circuit board, neuron replacement transplant, lesion closing, a repaired severed wire, or a guaranteed complete connection. No exact neuron count, circuit topology, molecular structures, numerical data, medical devices or actual microscopy.
Constraints: no text, letters, numbers, labels, arrows, logos or watermark. No people, patients or personal story. No imitation of a specific artist or published illustration. Make the small local young neuron visibly different in maturity and scale from the larger pre-existing neural architecture. Preserve that relation when viewed at thumbnail size.

cover.scope: Simplified hippocampal geometry, not microscopy, an anatomical wiring diagram, a treatment result or a patient image.
